purpose is to replace an unnecessarily strong microscopic target--uniform
real-frequency convergence of a retuned double-well susceptibility--by a
finite equilibrium correlation certificate. This theorem is conditional only

approximation. No measurement or efficient Gibbs sampler is assumed.

equally to all C_theta(s). Thus it cancels in every combination below.

# Inclusive heat response of a bounded nonlinear mechanical contact

The earlier conditional support calculations remain unchanged. The result

explicit equilibrium scattering contract. It does not yet identify a full
continuous double-well Hamiltonian with the Toulouse scaling model.

## 1. Physical contract and observable

Two identical, lossless, semi-infinite scalar leads have impedance Z>0 at
their ACTUAL terminal planes. Each endpoint has mass M/2, M>0. The only
interaction between endpoints is a time-independent stable potential V(Y),
where Y=u_R-u_L; it need not be harmonic or weak. There is no ground, hidden

Gaussian. The common displacement U=(u_L+u_R)/2 and the relative coordinate

    T = M Udot^2/2 + (M/4) Ydot^2/2.

B=M/4 and its Ohmic friction is Z/2. These are derived from the two terminal
coordinates, not parameters inferred from a two-state truncation.

below hold. Absolute common position has no Gibbs state on the infinite

# Root whole review: inclusive nonlinear noise/heat identity

25 October 2026. Internally verified/accepted at the mathematical scope of
INCLUSIVE_NOISE_TRANSPORT.md, SHA256
8dc86a11ab401d88886f7a331ec380203d9df87386678cb4040a0f1c39b366f8.
Root read every section and independently reconstructed the mechanical
mapping, quantum insertion, current, mass bound and spectral certificates.

The terminal kinetic and damping transformations give relative mass M/4,
friction Z/2 and S_o=-1-i omega Z chi_Y with the stated Fourier convention.
The common free-mass amplitude and reference planes are consistent.
At symmetric infinitesimal thermal bias the diagonal parity input states
are unchanged to first order; the off-diagonal covariance insertion alone
is needed. Quantum KMS, rather than classical Gaussian integration by parts,
identifies its full odd input/output correlator with coherent response.
The inclusive current therefore keeps all inelastic outputs. The stated
complete equilibrium scattering assumption is load-bearing; no general
asymptotic-completeness theorem for every potential has been smuggled in.

Equilibrium outgoing CCR plus KMS and Cauchy imply |S_o|<=1, the optical
disk inequality and 0<=T_eff<=1. Root separately computed
integral omega g_theta=6 zeta(3)theta^2. This verifies the UNIFORM relative
finite-common-mass error 9 zeta(3)Mtheta/(pi^2 Z), including retuned response
families, without an uncontrolled bound on Re chi.

The fluctuation-dissipation weight comparison gives the displayed constant
variance floor, with sharpness claimed only for a relaxed positive spectral
class. The compliance and canonical f-sum rules have the correct factors.
A static zero-frequency covariance only adds variance. The finite-window
noise certificate bounds unmeasured positive spectral mass using the total
variance cap and prices its actual in-band error and observation timescale.

Root read the relevant governing primary ancestry in Yamamoto et al.,
equations (2)--(8), https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13552 , and the series
inelastic-current discussion of Yeyati et al.,
https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13526 . No claim of inventing the general
current/admittance principle follows from the mechanical specialization.

Acceptance closes the inclusive-current, finite-common-mass, and stated
noise-inference mathematical gates under the explicit equilibrium scattering
contract. Iden
